entries.subject: ESA/Webb weic2207c
entries.finding: Southern Ring Nebula (MIRI Image): MIRI at 7.7, 11.3, 12 and 18 µm; 1306 × 1133 px over 2.39 × 2.07 arcmin, released 12 July 2022. The file's embedded sky tags for scale and direction, 0.1099 arcsec per pixel and north 124.65° right of vertical, and the star for place: the middle of the bright central star's saturated pixels, pixel 663.3, 553.5, is set at SIMBAD's place for NGC 3132, so the frame's centre is 151.7566982°, -40.4364794°. The tags alone put the star 0.29 arcsec away.

entries.subject: The walls under this picture
entries.finding: The same walls as the near-infrared dataset (src/objects/ngc-3132-layers): the density grid of Monteiro et al. (2025), placed on the sky as measured there. The grid is the ionised gas, from H-alpha and [N II] velocity cubes; this picture also holds dust and molecular light, which takes the same depths here. Run on this picture (packages/bake/authoring/ngc-3132/grid-fit.mts with this bank's id), the same fit finds the grid's second axis at 324.5 degrees, against 325.5 from the near-infrared picture, with a correlation of 0.58 (0.136 half a turn on, 0.316 with the other handedness): a second picture, taken with another instrument, gives the same turn within a degree. The walls keep the near-infrared picture's value.

entries.subject: The two stars at the centre
entries.finding: This picture shows two stars at the nebula's centre, 1.8 arcsec apart (measured here): the bright one the near-infrared picture shows, and a second one. The frame is placed by the bright one, the saturated patch nearest the place the picture's tags give SIMBAD's position; its own light, out to 2.1 arcsec, stays at the star. The second star lies in that light.
